**Finding: MISSING** (medium severity) — no post-termination transition assistance or data-return clause exists.

**What I found:**
- **Section 14 (Termination, p0079)** only requires TrueLink to keep providing Hosting and Support Services until the last day of the month following our termination notice — roughly 30–60 days of continued service, not migration help.
- **Section 13 (p0078)** confirms we retain ownership of our domains and Client Content and gives us 30/60 days to arrange a new name server and hosting environment — but it puts that burden entirely on *us* and imposes no obligation on TrueLink to return, export, or delete anything.
- **Section 10 (Confidentiality)** has no return-or-destroy provision at all, so even the partial substitute the planner anticipated is absent.
- Searches for return / export / delete / destroy / transition / machine-readable surfaced nothing relevant.

Because TrueLink hosts our Web Site, daily backups (§2(f)), and borrower/loan Credit Data, the rule clearly expects an exit clause here. Both the preferred and fallback positions fail, so an insertion is warranted rather than a rationale-only note.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** inserted the preferred position after §14 — (a) up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates including migration help; (b) return of Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days; (c) deletion thereafter from systems and backup media with written certification.

**Placement check:** siting the clause in §14 is effective post-termination because §24 (p0090) provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive expiration or termination.

The comment offers the 90-day assistance fallback in case six months proves difficult for TrueLink.
